summary:
The Pitcairn Islands stand under the United Kingdom's framework: defence and external affairs are reserved to the United Kingdom, and United Kingdom domestic measures such as the Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not apply here of their own force. Local law governs, and those measures could reach Pitcairn only by Order in Council.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001.

The Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, and that guarantee has been in force since 2010.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 14 May 2015. The Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 defines marriage as the union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity. The Island Council approved the ordinance unanimously on 1 April 2015, Governor Jonathan Sinclair signed it on 5 May 2015, and it was published on 13 May 2015.

The same ordinance recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn.

Adoption has been legal since 2015 and is open to married, unmarried and single people.
tangentialFactors:
Military service in the Pitcairn Islands falls under United Kingdom responsibility rather than local control, so any service eligibility rules a visitor might compare against are set outside the territory.

The resident population is roughly 50 people, and none is known to be in a same-sex relationship. With no visible local same-sex couples, social exposure risk for a visitor rests on personal disclosure rather than on observed community precedent.

The territory is indexed within United Kingdom LGBT-rights timelines, which is a comparative framing used by the source rather than a statement about how United Kingdom law operates on the ground here.
localsOnly:
Residents are covered by the constitutional prohibition on discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation contained in the Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010, which has applied since that order came into force.

Residents may marry without distinction as to sex or gender under the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015, and civil partnerships formed outside Pitcairn are recognised locally.

Adoption is available to married, unmarried and single residents alike under the 2015 adoption provisions.

Legislation of this kind originates with the Island Council, which approved the 2015 ordinance without dissent before it received the Governor's signature and publication.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in the inventory addresses legal gender recognition, change of sex markers on passports or birth records, entry or visa screening that could disclose a trans identity, access to gender-affirming healthcare, or facilities rules. Whether any such provision exists locally is unresolved on this inventory.

The enforcement record of the 2010 non-discrimination guarantee is not sourced: no complaint, ruling or reported case involving sexual orientation discrimination appears in the inventory, and the absence of such material is not evidence that the guarantee has been tested.

Whether United Kingdom measures such as the Equality Act 2010 or the 2025 single-sex-services code could be extended to Pitcairn by Order in Council, and on what terms, is unresolved here; the inventory states only that they do not apply of their own force.

Whether the 2015 ordinance or the Constitution Order contains any provision expressly referring to gender identity beyond the marriage definition is not sourced and remains unresolved.
